fullPassage: Economists like teaching about taxes and subsidies because they don't "stick" where they "land". Some of a tax's burden or a subsidy's benefit passes from those who write or cash the check to other market participants because taxes and subsidies change people's behavior. Buyers might bear the brunt of a tax legally paid by sellers and vice versa. Who is legally responsible for writing the check doesn't matter. How suppliers and demanders respond to changing prices does. Cigarette buyers tend to be less price-sensitive than sellers. When large tobacco companies get taxed, the cigarette supply shrinks. Smokers pay higher prices, but most don't cut back much because they aren't especially price-sensitive. Cigarette taxes land on huge corporations with a great amount of cash but stick to disproportionately poor smokers.

❌ ③ who: 선행사 those(사람)의 주격 관계대명사 — 적절.
✅ ④ behaviors: behavior는 '행동 방식'을 의미하는 불가산명사로 쓰임이 일반적. 원문도 behavior(단수). behaviors → behavior.

det.korean: 세금 부담은 가격 변화에 덜 반응하는 쪽에 전가되며, 회사에 부과된 세금이 가격에 덜 민감한 흡연자들이 궁극적으로 부담하는 것에서 볼 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① The burden of a tax falls on the party less responsive to price changes, as seen when taxes on companies are ultimately paid by less price-sensitive smokers.: 가격 덜 민감한 쪽이 부담 + 담배세 사례 = 정확한 요약.
❌ ② Governments should always impose taxes on consumers rather than companies to ensure fairness.: '항상 소비자에게 과세'는 본문이 제안하는 바가 아님.
❌ ③ Wealthy corporations always manage to transfer the entire tax burden to their customers.: '항상 전체 부담' 전가는 과장.
❌ ④ The concept of tax subsidies is irrelevant to modern economic theory.: 보조금이 무관하다는 건 본문과 반대.
det.tip: 요약 핵심: less responsive = 더 부담. 담배세 = 가난한 흡연자 부담.

(힌트: '중요하다'라는 뜻의 동사. m으로 시작)

det.analysis: 앞 조동사 doesn't 뒤 동사원형. matter = 중요하다. 법적 책임자는 중요하지 않다는 원문.
det.tip: matter(동사: 중요하다) = make a difference, be important. It doesn't matter = 중요하지 않다.
